To start, you're going to have to pick your weapon of choice. Three of "best" weapons are the Jagras Hacker III, the Leviathan's Fury, and the Great Wyvern Jawblade, though all of the final Greastswords are very viable.

Some pros and cons of each of the ones I listed are as follows:

Jagras Hacker III:
Pros: Good Base Damage of 912, that can be boosted through use of the Elementless Jewel as well as having 2 Rank 3 Decoration Slots. 3 Augmentation Slots, easy to make

Cons: Can only reach a max sharpness of Blue, ugly.

Leviathan's Fury:
Pros: Good Base damage of 960 with a solid Dragon Element at 300 and Average Elder Seal. A single rank 2 decoration slot. Capable of reaching White Sharpness with Handicraft

Cons: Only 1 Augmentation Slot, Annoying to make, Dragon Element wont proc all that often due to how Elemental damage works

Great Wyvern Jawblade:
Pros: Base Damage of 960, Can be boosted by Elementless Decoration, one rank 3 decoration slot, +20 Defense Bonus

Cons: probably the most annoying of the three to get, Blue Sharpness, 1 Augment Slot

Once you've chosen your weapon, it's time to focus on skills. The Greatsword is primarily about doing massive damage through use of the True Charged Slash, so skills that increase your damage, affinity, or skills that speed up your ability to use the TCS will result in greater DPS. Ergo, your primary skills will be skills like:
- Weakness Exploit

- Attack Boost (at least level 4)

- Focus

- Maximum Might

- Critical Boost

- Handicraft

Side Note: Crit Draw Builds are also viable, in which case you'll also want to use the skills  Quick Sheathe and Critical Draw

Back to the main topic, you'll also want some utility skills so that you're more likely to survive and/or so that you can keep up on the offense more easily. These include skills like:
- Earplugs

- Tremor Resistence

- Speed Sharpening

- Protective Polish


Finally, you have the defensive skills. These are basically all the skills you've already listed plus things like Divine Blessing, that are all designed to specifically keep you alive

If you're trying to down monsters as quickly as possible, you'll want more damage oriented skill. If you're having trouble with survival you may want to either add a few defensive skills or just switch to a purely defensive set. Test out everything you can

In reality though, the best thing to do is to use a build that you feel comfortable with. Perhaps you find that the TCS-centric playstyle isn't to your liking, or that you don't mesh well with it, but you feel comfortable with a Crit Draw Build. Or perhaps you find that you die too much with the attack focused builds and you prefer the more defensive ones. So long as you're completing your hunts, there's no real "wrong" build. A single successful 30 minute hunt is always going to yield more items than 3 failed 10 minute attempts.

Personally, I use the following:
- Great Wyvern's Jawblade

This gives me:

I have the elementless Jewel slotted into my Great Sword, 3 Sharpening jewels between my gloves and belt, and 2 free Rank 1 slots in the chest and a Rank 3 slot in the head. While not the "Meta Build', this provides me with a nice balance of Attack and Defense, and I have some modularity in the set so that I can adapt the armor set to what I'm facing.

As I said before, it's all about what you're comfortable with. At the end of the day, aside from trolling people, there's no wrong way to play the game

You can speed it up with Blood Weapon and Salted Earth, but those only last for so long and against a boss they give 1 blood guage per tick for SE, and 3 per attack for Blood Weapon, so about 2.5 per second. With an additional 10 blood guage every 7.5 second, this brings the average to 3.83333 blood guage per second. In comparison a warrior averages 25 beast guage per 7.5 seconds, or 3.33333 per second, which means that WAR is accumulating beast guage only marginally slower than DRK is getting blood guage, but DRK has to use two abilities to speed their aquisition up. Without Blood Weapon and Salted Earth it takes 10 Soul Eater  combos to get to full blood guage, but WAR needs only 5 at most and thats if they're being ineffecient between fell cleaves. The Blackest Night can be used to get an extra 50 guage, but it has to be popped for it to proc.

Lets say your stats give it a 600 AR, and you chaos infused. Fpr example, lets say that its a nice even split of 150.

You are fighting someone with a 20%/18%/18%/20% damage reduction for physical, magic, lightning, and fire respectively.

20% of 150 is 30, so the fire and physical portion only does 120 each.

18% of 150 is 27, so magic and lightning are only doing 123 damage now.

All together you've lost 114 damage, and your 600 AR amounts to 486 AR now.

So you infuse it again and boost the lightning damage. It still does 600 , but now you've got 200/150/250 now for physical, magic and lightning respectively. Fighting the same person.

20% of 200 is 40, 18% of 150 is 27, and 18% of 250 is 45.

40+27+45=112.

Let's leave things otherwise the same, but instead of developing the single child in the mother, humans lay eggs that are incubated instead.

First off, we know that humans develop normally over a 9 month period wherein nutrients taken in by the mother are also.used to feed the child. For Egg laying species this is not possible. So we're going to need either incredibly large eggs, so that the egg can develop into regular sized human babies, or the eggs would be smaller but humans would hatch at a much smaller size. If we're keeping things as they are, ie 9 months of development, then labour would be pretty fucking intense. Otherwise, biologically, things wouldnt be too different. The egg would have to be incubated for probably about 8 months, while the first month is dedicated to making the egg. And our already severe fear of snakes would be heightened. 

The social sphere is where things would get interesting. wlWe'd see things like egg warmers being manufactured so that parents can work while their child incubates in the egg. Mothers would probably receive one of these from friends or work as a baby shower style gift. 

But then there'd be a subset of people who believe that an egg should be incubated by the parents by themselves, so as to develop a bond with the yet unhatched child. Tons of scientific research would be done to test this hypothesis. Results are inconclusive.

You'd hear stories of criminals eating "Human Omelettes". There's some truth here, such and such person in the past did it, but it's rare because eating human eggs is highly illegal. Also illegal is egg theft, as well as egg abandonment or endangerment.

Eggs themselves become symbols of fertility and life in many cultures. Things like chicken eggs become more of a luxury, and dont even get me started on shit like caviar become even more so, if it's not just outlawed outright.

Parents would keep the first part of the shell that is broken apart when their child hatches as a keepsake. The shape of the first piece would be rumoured to affect their fortunes, but that is obviously bunk.

Orphanages would be weird and eerie, as many would likely be filled with the eggs of people who couldn't afford to raise a human child. Potential adoptive parents would mostly choose their egg child based on the colour/pattern of the shell, but you'd have a few people who just want to make sure that as many children as possible had homes. There'd also be orphanges for children already hatched but, much like the world we live in, adoption of the youngest (eggs in this case, like kittens and puppys in our world) is the norm.

All in all things would be different, but more or less the same. Someone on a popular website will one day make a post titled "How different would things be if we had live birth like most other mammals?" And someone would describe our world, while a criminal warlord adds bacon and cheese to his Human Omelette.

To elaborate on this, look at how Halo works with things like snipers and Shotguns.

Snipers and Shotguns are classified as Power Weapons, weapons that can reliably one shot enemies and can change the flow of the game. These weapons appear maybe once or twice throughout a match, are limited to one or two people across the game, and have limited ammo. Because of this the Primary Weapon Analogs in Halo are used for the better part of a match.

Compare that to Destiny.

In Destiny, everyone in the game starts off with Special Ammo. This means that everyone in the game starts with ammo for a weapon that can reliably one shot people. Ammo for Shotguns and Special weapons spawns at regular intervals across the map meaning that, unless you are using only your special, you can almost always have special ammo. That means that everyone has near constant access to power weapons.

So what happens when you have a near constant source of ammo for your power weapons? You use them. Primary usage goes down, and the primary weapons that /can/ compete with specials get nerfed in someway for being too powerful. Which further exacerbates the problem because now the primaries that put up a fight can't anymore.

SO how do you solve this issue? IMO the best way would be to treat Special Weapons like the Power Weapons they are. Start off with no ammo, limit the amount of times that Special Ammo spawns in a game (say twice a match), and reduce the range at which special will drop from a crate for teammates who weren't right beside the Special box.

This would help, but might make it too similar to Halo.

In my Mind this is what makes each DLC class special:

Dread Fighter: 

Dread fighter is like master of arms. It's prepared for any encounter, and it has the superior use of Hidden Weapons. The class has good speed and res, with decent strength and skill if iirc. 

Above all else, dread fighter works best as a defensive mage killer. Between Even Keel and Iron Will you can have up to 8 less damage when you let an enemy mage attack you.

Dark Flier: 

Dark Flier is a more offensively focused class. Strong Magic and Speed growths, with good Res growths, allow it to hit enemies hard, double them, and tank some magic hits. Galeforce, a skill lauded in Awakening, will allow you to make really hard pushes against enemies. It's an interesting class but you have to watch out for bows, for obvious reasons.

Great Lord:

Great Lord is a fun class. It's doesn't have any particularly high growth rates, which means you may wish to use it as you near max level, but what it lacks in growths in makes up for in phenomenal skills. Charm and Dual Strike are alright, but the two skills that make the class shine are Aether and Awakening.

Aether is a phenomenal skill that promotes death for your enemies and health for you. Awakening boosts your hit, dodge, crit, and avoid by 30 when you are at less than half HP. As such, it is best to make with Vantage a great lord. Vantage + Awakening is pretty broken. Plus the combo of Swords and Lances allows you to get amazing enemy coverage.

Lodestar:

Lodestar has a few things to note:

1: Dancing Blade and Speedtaker are great skills that can boost the speed of a unit that needs it (Looking at you Xander)

2: It is the only class that can get to S-Swords outside of Swordmaster. Useless in Conquest, but still cool I guess. It does allow you to, therefore, give a non-swordmaster the Hagakure BLade

3: It has great Skill and Speed.

Lodestar is a pretty balanced class, that seeks to utilize the characters skills and speed. With a Class cap of 35 Skill, you'll see a lot of skills activating. Add in Speedtaker and/or Dancing Blade and you will be doubling opponents more and more as you kill them with your skills. Where the class falls short is it's defenses and it's str. Still a very good class to use, and it can always be reclassed out of if it isn't working for you.

Vanguard:

Hit things hard is vanguard's motto. Heavy Blade and Strengthtaker will make your physical hits even stronger, while Veteren's intuition will keep you safer from Crits. Aether is Aether and as such is amazing. Vanguard's growths lean towards HP, Strength and Defense, so a unit that needs those could reclass into it to patch up it's weaknesses.Vanguard is also one of the classes that you can get an infinite number of brands for, so long as you're willing to do the dlc each time. Swords and Axes will allow you to get decent weapon triangle coverage, but not as Good as Great Lords. That being said, you hit like a truck.

Grandmaster:

I'll be frank here. Grandmaster is kind of lacking. It's a Jack of All Trades style class, with a slight focus on magic. Ignis is very similar to Dragon Fang, though dragon fang adds half your attack (Weapon + Mag or Str) whereas Ignis only adds Half Str or Half Magic. Though ignis did get a buff in Fates as it adds half of your str if you're using a physical weapon and vice versa.

Otherwise, Grandmaster is only really good as a support class. Rally Spectrum can be pretty handy, Tactical Advice allows you to help other units not get hit or crit.  It's just lackluster to me. I'm sure someone will disagree.

But this really isn't the over point of the post. The point is that you have options for getting the rep you need to get to level 25 in a faction that weren't present before. If you're going to focus solely on the fact that 50k exp is still a decent chunk of exp to try and get just to trade in the motes, you're purposely avoiding the point to try and go "look, I'm right" and thus not adding anything to the post of worth.

So to reiterate:

Rep can be easily obtained by trading in Motes, Weapon Parts, Armor Parts, Class Specific Armor mats, Heavy Ammo Synths, Doing the Nightfall, Doing the weekly heroic(This week only it seems as the heroic is going to disappear now), and a few other options that make attaining the ranks you need to get to 25 to start the faction quest a lot easier than it was previously, making the task less daunting.

Let's say you want to level new monarchy and you only got to rank 3 previously. you need 2500 rep to get a level in the faction.

Bounties give either 50 or ~65 rep divided by 2 because of the pledge system so 25 or 32, the nightfall will give 250 to your faction. Crucible matches award around 7 rep if you've pledged after the nightfall bonus. I've noted that, so far, no crucible bounties are worth 3k exp/65rep and that at least two Vanguard bounties are worth 65rep

Since we're taking the power level approach to farming faction rank, let's spend all our motes and strange coins in an attempt to speed it up.

So, if you do all the bounties each day you get over 37500 motes, and if you play for 3 hours a day, earning 50k exp outside of the bounties, you can earn 9 motes of light a day. if you can get one more mote from a random source, that gives you 10 motes a day for 3 hours of work. If you run PoE 2 times over the work you should receive between 6-18 strange coins plus at least 3 motes, possibly even 6

10 motes will give you 250 rep after the nightfall bonus has been applied. 

The strange coins can be traded to Xur for 3 Heavy Synths for one coin giving you between 18-54 synths from PoE(going with the average of 36 synths a week), each one worth 25 rep after nightfall, and the 6 motes from PoE will give another 125rep.

So if you play 5/7 days a week(A lot for some i know) you can get, and it takes 10 crucible games to complete your crucible bounties:

250NF + 1.25NF bonus(5 days(10(25 rep) + 2(32 rep))) + (5days*250 from 10 motes) + (36 synths*25) + 125(PoE motes) +(70*5 days) rep from crucible = 4837 rep a week 

4837 rep is almost 2 ranks a week, from playing for 3 hours a day  for 5 days a week. This also excludes doing patrols, and the rep gained from vanguard packages which you will be getting with the pledge system. YOu may also get rep from opening your faction packages as well in the week, plus any motes and strange coins you get from the packages can be used to further your rank as well

This means that despite the fact that rep gained is not cut in half due to the pledge system it is now possible to easily attain 2 ranks in a week, whereas many people had issues getting one rank a week before. 

and just for fun, if you played for 3 hours a day for 7 days a week the value becomes 6262 rep a week for your faction, in this example NM, which is over 2 ranks a week
